definition: **Trade dispute** — dispute between employers and workmen or among workmen connected with employment, non-employment, terms, or conditions. Registered unions acting **in contemplation or furtherance** of a trade dispute enjoy **immunities**: (1) **Criminal** — certain agreements in restraint of trade not prosecuted as criminal conspiracy; (2) **Civil** — limited protection from tort claims (e.g. inducement of breach) when dispute-related. Immunities are **conditional**— unlawful objectives or violence fall outside protection.

statutoryReferences.note: Cross-read with general law of conspiracy and tort

examChecklist.text: Explain **criminal immunity** (concerted action, registered union, bona fide dispute)
Explain **civil immunity** limits; when immunities **do not apply** (malice, unlawful means, unrelated acts)
